summary.text: Diana Ayala is a former New York City Council Member who represented District 8 (East Harlem and parts of the South Bronx) for eight years, from 2018 to 2026, including as Deputy Speaker and as chair of the General Welfare and Mental Health, Disabilities and Addictions committees. Before the Council she worked as a senior center program director and as a constituent-services director and deputy chief of staff for Council Speaker Melissa Mark-Viverito. She won the June 2026 Democratic primary for the open Assembly District 68 seat over incumbent Eddie Gibbs and is the only candidate listed on the November ballot; her campaign says she is running on affordability, housing, mental health care, immigrant protections and workers' rights.

paragraphs.text: According to Wikipedia, Ayala was born in Río Piedras, Puerto Rico, in 1973 and moved to New York City with her family as a child. Her campaign website describes her as a lifelong New Yorker and the daughter of Puerto Rican parents.

Ayala earned a degree in human services from Bronx Borough Community College and studied sociology at CUNY Herbert H. Lehman College; her campaign website describes her as a graduate of both institutions.

Before elected office, she worked as a program director at the Carver Senior Center, a caseworker at Corsi Houses, and constituent-services director and then deputy chief of staff to Council Speaker Melissa Mark-Viverito.

In 2017 she ran for the open District 8 Council seat when Mark-Viverito was term-limited, winning the Democratic primary over Robert Rodriguez, then an Assemblymember, and three other candidates, and the general election over Republican and Conservative candidates.
She served on the New York City Council representing District 8 (East Harlem and parts of the South Bronx) from January 2018 until January 2026, and was re-elected in 2021 and 2023.

In the Council she chaired the General Welfare Committee and the Mental Health, Disabilities and Addictions Committee, according to her campaign website. City & State reports she served as deputy speaker under Speaker Adrienne Adams for the last four years of her tenure after briefly running for speaker herself.

As General Welfare chair, she says she helped expand the CityFHEPS rental-assistance voucher program and worked to create and preserve affordable housing in the district; she also says she helped secure major capital investments for Metropolitan Hospital in East Harlem.

In February 2026 she filed to run for Assembly District 68 against incumbent Assemblymember Eddie Gibbs, and on June 23, 2026 she won the Democratic primary with 51.9% of the vote to Gibbs' 31.2%; she also holds the Working Families Party line.
According to Wikipedia, she lives in East Harlem and has four children and three grandchildren.
